evidence.claim: The flagged transaction 3478782 ($292.36, online, product C, 2016-11-22 17:27:07) is about 2.4x the card's prior maximum amount ($121.32) and about 6x its prior median ($47.29) computed over the 35 transactions before opening.

The card was dormant for about 16 days before the flagged transaction (the only entry in the 72h card_window is the flagged transaction itself, gap_seconds 1,446,851 from the prior transaction), then jumped straight to $292.36 with no smaller online purchases in between.

Card C11891-K1 has one prior confirmed-fraud closed case, CC-4160 (pattern card_not_present_fraud, exposure $90.54, closed 2016-09-30), the same channel as the flagged transaction and within about 53 days of it.

The case-memory calibration scores the flagged transaction at cms_p 0.6595 (calibrated 0.7533), and after the prior-fraud adjustment the engine probability is 0.8343, close to but distinct from the real-time model's risk_score of 0.79.
The purchaser/recipient email domain hotmail.com has been used 7 times before on this card out of the 35 prior transactions, so it is a familiar domain rather than a brand-new one.

case.summary: Verdict: fraud, probability 0.92, pattern card_not_present_fraud - a single $292.36 online purchase (txn 3478782, sole member of the episode, exposure $292.36) far above the card's prior baseline, on a card with a prior confirmed CNP-fraud case. A customer_validation request was sent and the customer denied making the purchase, which settled the question under R2; without that denial the amount jump alone would read as ambiguous single-purchase CNP activity. Recommended: CREATE_CASE (auto) and BLOCK_CARD (L1, awaiting approval).
